stem: In the figure, line $m$ is parallel to line $n$. What is the value of $x$?
stimulus: A nutrition science student sketches the layout of a food label. The top and bottom borders of the nutrient panel lie on parallel lines $m$ and $n$, and a slanted divider runs across both borders along line $t$. Where line $t$ meets line $m$, the angle above line $m$ and to the right of line $t$ measures $(3x + 15)^\circ$. Where line $t$ meets line $n$, the angle below line $n$ and to the left of line $t$ measures $(5x - 25)^\circ$. Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
explanation: The two marked angles sit outside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are alternate exterior angles and have equal measures. Set $3x + 15 = 5x - 25$, which gives $40 = 2x$, so $x = 20$.

B.why: You treated the angles as supplementary and solved $(3x + 15) + (5x - 25) = 180$. Alternate exterior angles are equal. They do not add to 180.

C.why: You found $x = 20$ and then gave the angle measure $3(20) + 15 = 75$. The question asks for $x$, not the angle.

D.why: You gave $180 - 75 = 105$, which is the measure of the angle next to a marked angle. The question asks for $x$.

stem: In the figure, two lines intersect. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle labeled $(7x - 6)^\circ$?
stimulus: On a city map, a cartographer draws two straight roads that cross at a single intersection. The roads form four angles. Two of these angles are next to each other along the same road: one is labeled $(7x - 6)^\circ$ and the other is labeled $(3x + 16)^\circ$. Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
explanation: The two angles are next to each other along one straight road, so they form a linear pair and add to 180. Solve $(7x - 6) + (3x + 16) = 180$: you get $10x + 10 = 180$, so $x = 17$. The labeled angle measures $7(17) - 6 = 113$ degrees.

A.why: You correctly found $x = 17$ but stopped there. You still need to substitute it into $7x - 6$ to get the angle measure.

B.why: You set the angles equal, as if they were vertical angles. That gives $x = 5.5$ and $7(5.5) - 6 = 32.5$. Adjacent angles along a straight line are supplementary, not equal.

C.why: You found the measure of the other angle, $3(17) + 16 = 67$, rather than the angle labeled $(7x - 6)^\circ$.

stem: In the figure, line $p$ is parallel to line $q$. What is the value of $x$?
stimulus: A sports scientist marks two parallel sprint lanes on a training field, along lines $p$ and $q$. A diagonal agility line crosses both lanes along line $k$. Both marked angles are between lines $p$ and $q$ and on the left side of line $k$. The angle at line $p$ measures $(2x + 8)^\circ$, and the angle at line $q$ measures $(4x - 20)^\circ$. Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
explanation: Both angles lie between the parallel lines and on the same side of the transversal, so they are same-side interior angles and add to 180. Solve $(2x + 8) + (4x - 20) = 180$: you get $6x - 12 = 180$, so $6x = 192$ and $x = 32$.

A.why: You set the angles equal and solved $2x + 8 = 4x - 20$. Same-side interior angles are supplementary, not equal.

B.why: You set the sum equal to 90 instead of 180, as if the angles were complementary, and solved $6x - 12 = 90$.

D.why: You found $x = 32$ and then gave the angle measure $2(32) + 8 = 72$. The question asks for $x$.

stem: In the figure, line $r$ is parallel to line $s$. What is the value of $x$?
stimulus: A textile historian diagrams a section of handwoven cloth. Two parallel warp threads run along lines $r$ and $s$, and one slanted weft thread crosses both of them along line $w$. Where line $w$ meets line $r$, the angle above line $r$ and to the left of line $w$ measures $118^\circ$. Where line $w$ meets line $s$, the angle above line $s$ and to the left of line $w$ measures $(2x + 6)^\circ$. Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
explanation: The two angles are in the same position at each intersection (above the line, left of the transversal), so they are corresponding angles and are equal. Solve $2x + 6 = 118$: you get $2x = 112$, so $x = 56$.

A.why: You treated the angles as supplementary, so you set $2x + 6 = 180 - 118 = 62$ and got $x = 28$. Corresponding angles are equal.

C.why: You added 6 to 118 instead of subtracting it, which gave $2x = 124$ and $x = 62$.

D.why: You gave the angle measure, $118$, which is what $2x + 6$ equals. The question asks for $x$.

stem: In the figure, line $a$ is parallel to line $b$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle labeled $(4x + 22)^\circ$?
stimulus: An ornithologist draws two parallel power lines where swallows perch, along lines $a$ and $b$, with line $a$ above line $b$. A straight support cable crosses both power lines along line $c$. Where line $c$ meets line $a$, the angle below line $a$ and to the right of line $c$ measures $(6x - 14)^\circ$. Where line $c$ meets line $b$, the angle above line $b$ and to the left of line $c$ measures $(4x + 22)^\circ$. Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
explanation: Both angles lie between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are alternate interior angles and are equal. Solve $6x - 14 = 4x + 22$: you get $2x = 36$, so $x = 18$. The labeled angle measures $4(18) + 22 = 94$ degrees.

A.why: You correctly found $x = 18$ but stopped there. You still need to substitute it into $4x + 22$ to get the angle measure.

B.why: You subtracted the constants the wrong way, writing $2x = 22 - 14$. That gave $x = 4$ and an angle of $4(4) + 22 = 38$.

C.why: You gave $180 - 94 = 86$, which is the measure of the angle supplementary to the labeled angle. Alternate interior angles are equal, so the labeled angle is 94, not 86.
